children: The FTSE 100 fell around 0.3% on Monday, weighed down by weakness in major consumer stocks, with Unilever and BAT declining 1.6% and 1.5%, respectively.
The losses were partly offset by gains in energy shares, as Shell and BP rose 0.7% and 1.5% alongside higher crude prices.
Investor focus remained firmly on developments in the US-Iran conflict, with tensions persisting after reports that the US had struck three Iranian oil tankers following attacks on US warships.
Energy Secretary Chris Wright also warned that a new nuclear agreement with Tehran may not be reached soon, suggesting Washington could instead focus on eliminating Iran’s nuclear capabilities.
Meanwhile, domestic data showed UK house prices fell 0.2% in August, pushing annual prices into negative territory for the first time since November 2023, according to Lloyds.

title: FTSE 100 Trades Lower
